kinds.description: APIGroup contains the name, the supported versions, and the preferred version of a group.

kinds.name: APIVersions
kinds.description: APIVersions lists the versions that are available, to allow clients to discover the API at /api, which is the root path of the legacy v1 API.

kinds.name: Binding
kinds.description: Binding ties one object to another; for example, a pod is bound to a node by a scheduler.

kinds.description: ComponentStatus (and ComponentStatusList) holds the cluster validation info. Deprecated: This API is deprecated in v1.19+

kinds.name: ConfigMap
kinds.description: ConfigMap holds configuration data for pods to consume.

Events should be treated as informative, best-effort, supplemental data.

kinds.name: LimitRange
kinds.description: LimitRange sets resource usage limits for each kind of resource in a Namespace.

kinds.name: Namespace

kinds.name: Node
kinds.description: Node is a worker node in Kubernetes. Each node will have a unique identifier in the cache (i.e. in etcd).

kinds.name: PersistentVolume

kinds.name: PersistentVolumeClaim

kinds.name: Pod

kinds.name: PodTemplate
kinds.description: PodTemplate describes a template for creating copies of a predefined pod.

kinds.description: ResourceQuota sets aggregate quota restrictions enforced per namespace

kinds.name: Secret
kinds.description: Secret holds secret data of a certain type. The total bytes of the values in the Data field must be less than MaxSecretSize bytes.

kinds.name: Service
kinds.description: Service is a named abstraction of software service (for example, mysql) consisting of local port (for example 3306) that the proxy listens on, and the selector that determines which pods will answer requests sent through the proxy.

relationships.description: Routes traffic to Pods via label selector

kinds.name: ServiceAccount
kinds.description: ServiceAccount binds together: * a name, understood by users, and perhaps by peripheral systems, for an identity * a principal that can be authenticated and authorized * a set of secrets

kinds.name: Status

kinds.name: WatchEvent

kinds.description: CustomResourceDefinition represents a resource that should be exposed on the API server.  Its name MUST be in the format <.spec.name>.<.spec.group>.

kinds.name: APIService
kinds.description: APIService represents a server for a particular GroupVersion. Name must be "version.group".

kinds.name: DaemonSet
kinds.description: DaemonSet represents the configuration of a daemon set.

kinds.name: Deployment
kinds.description: Deployment enables declarative updates for Pods and ReplicaSets.

kinds.name: ReplicaSet
kinds.description: ReplicaSet ensures that a specified number of pod replicas are running at any given time.

kinds.name: StatefulSet
kinds.description:
StatefulSet represents a set of pods with consistent identities. Identities are defined as:
  - Network: A single stable DNS and hostname.
  - Storage: As many VolumeClaims as requested.

The StatefulSet guarantees that a given network identity will always map to the same storage identity.

kinds.name: SelfSubjectReview
kinds.description: SelfSubjectReview contains the user information that the kube-apiserver has about the user making this request. When using impersonation, users will receive the user info of the user being impersonated.  If impersonation or request header authentication is used, any extra keys will have their case ignored and returned as lowercase.

kinds.name: TokenRequest
kinds.description: TokenRequest requests a token for a given service account.

kinds.name: TokenReview
kinds.description: TokenReview attempts to authenticate a token to a known user. Note: TokenReview requests may be cached by the webhook token authenticator plugin in the kube-apiserver.

kinds.name: LocalSubjectAccessReview
kinds.description: LocalSubjectAccessReview checks whether or not a user or group can perform an action in a given namespace. Having a namespace scoped resource makes it much easier to grant namespace scoped policy that includes permissions checking.

kinds.name: SelfSubjectAccessReview
kinds.description: SelfSubjectAccessReview checks whether or the current user can perform an action.  Not filling in a spec.namespace means "in all namespaces".  Self is a special case, because users should always be able to check whether they can perform an action

kinds.name: SelfSubjectRulesReview
kinds.description: SelfSubjectRulesReview enumerates the set of actions the current user can perform within a namespace. The returned list of actions may be incomplete depending on the server's authorization mode, and any errors experienced during the evaluation. SelfSubjectRulesReview should be used by UIs to show/hide actions, or to quickly let an end user reason about their permissions. kinds.name: SubjectAccessReview
kinds.description: SubjectAccessReview checks whether or not a user or group can perform an action.

kinds.name: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
kinds.description: HorizontalPodAutoscaler is the configuration for a horizontal pod autoscaler, which automatically manages the replica count of any resource implementing the scale subresource based on the metrics specified.

kinds.name: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
kinds.description: configuration of a horizontal pod autoscaler.

kinds.name: Scale
kinds.description: Scale represents a scaling request for a resource.

kinds.description: CronJob represents the configuration of a single cron job.

groups.name: discovery.k8s.io
groups.description: Endpoint slices for scalable service discovery

kinds.name: EndpointSlice
kinds.description: EndpointSlice represents a set of service endpoints. Most EndpointSlices are created by the EndpointSlice controller to represent the Pods selected by Service objects. For a given service there may be multiple EndpointSlice objects which must be joined to produce the full set of endpoints; you can find all of the slices for a given service by listing EndpointSlices in the service's namespace whose `kubernetes.io/service-name` label contains the service's name.

kinds.name: Event
kinds.description: Event is a report of an event somewhere in the cluster. It generally denotes some state change in the system. Events have a limited retention time and triggers and messages may evolve with time.  Event consumers should not rely on the timing of an event with a given Reason reflecting a consistent underlying trigger, or the continued existence of events with that Reason.  Events should be treated as informative, best-effort, supplemental data.

groups.name: flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io
groups.description: API server request prioritization and fairness

kinds.name: FlowSchema
kinds.description: FlowSchema defines the schema of a group of flows. Note that a flow is made up of a set of inbound API requests with similar attributes and is identified by a pair of strings: the name of the FlowSchema and a "flow distinguisher".

kinds.name: PriorityLevelConfiguration
kinds.description: PriorityLevelConfiguration represents the configuration of a priority level.

kinds.name: StorageVersion
kinds.description: Storage version of a specific resource.

groups.name: networking.k8s.io
groups.description: Network policies, Ingress, and service mesh configurations

kinds.name: IPAddress
kinds.description: IPAddress represents a single IP of a single IP Family. The object is designed to be used by APIs that operate on IP addresses. The object is used by the Service core API for allocation of IP addresses. An IP address can be represented in different formats, to guarantee the uniqueness of the IP, the name of the object is the IP address in canonical format, four decimal digits separated by dots suppressing leading zeros for IPv4 and the representation defined by RFC 5952 for IPv6. Valid: 192.168.

kinds.name: ServiceCIDR
kinds.description: ServiceCIDR defines a range of IP addresses using CIDR format (e.g. 192.168.0.0/24 or 2001:db2::/64). This range is used to allocate ClusterIPs to Service objects.

kinds.name: IPAddress

The object is used by the Service core API for allocation of IP addresses. An IP address can be represented in different formats, to guarantee the uniqueness of the IP, the name of the object is the IP address in canonical format, four decimal digits separated by dots suppressing leading zeros for IPv4 and the representation defined by RFC 5952 for IPv6. Valid: 192.168.

kinds.name: Ingress
kinds.description: Ingress is a collection of rules that allow inbound connections to reach the endpoints defined by a backend. An Ingress can be configured to give services externally-reachable urls, load balance traffic, terminate SSL, offer name based virtual hosting etc.

kinds.name: IngressClass
kinds.description: IngressClass represents the class of the Ingress, referenced by the Ingress Spec. The `ingressclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class` annotation can be used to indicate that an IngressClass should be considered default. When a single IngressClass resource has this annotation set to true, new Ingress resources without a class specified will be assigned this default class.

kinds.name: NetworkPolicy
kinds.description: NetworkPolicy describes what network traffic is allowed for a set of Pods

kinds.name: ServiceCIDR
kinds.description: ServiceCIDR defines a range of IP addresses using CIDR format (e.g. 192.168.0.0/24 or 2001:db2::/64). This range is used to allocate ClusterIPs to Service objects.

kinds.name: RuntimeClass
kinds.description: RuntimeClass defines a class of container runtime supported in the cluster. The RuntimeClass is used to determine which container runtime is used to run all containers in a pod. RuntimeClasses are manually defined by a user or cluster provisioner, and referenced in the PodSpec. The Kubelet is responsible for resolving the RuntimeClassName reference before running the pod.  For more details, see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/runtime-class/

kinds.name: Eviction
kinds.description: Eviction evicts a pod from its node subject to certain policies and safety constraints. This is a subresource of Pod.  A request to cause such an eviction is created by POSTing to .../pods/<pod name>/evictions.

kinds.name: PodDisruptionBudget
kinds.description: PodDisruptionBudget is an object to define the max disruption that can be caused to a collection of pods

groups.name: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
groups.description: Role-based access control for Kubernetes resources

kinds.name: ClusterRole
kinds.description: ClusterRole is a cluster level, logical grouping of PolicyRules that can be referenced as a unit by a RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding.

kinds.name: ClusterRoleBinding
kinds.description: ClusterRoleBinding references a ClusterRole, but not contain it.  It can reference a ClusterRole in the global namespace, and adds who information via Subject.

kinds.name: Role
kinds.description: Role is a namespaced, logical grouping of PolicyRules that can be referenced as a unit by a RoleBinding.

kinds.name: RoleBinding
kinds.description: RoleBinding references a role, but does not contain it.  It can reference a Role in the same namespace or a ClusterRole in the global namespace. It adds who information via Subjects and namespace information by which namespace it exists in.  RoleBindings in a given namespace only have effect in that namespace.

kinds.name: DeviceClass
kinds.description:
DeviceClass is a vendor- or admin-provided resource that contains device configuration and selectors. It can be referenced in the device requests of a claim to apply these presets. Cluster scoped.

This is an alpha type and requires enabling the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate.

kinds.name: DeviceTaintRule
kinds.description: DeviceTaintRule adds one taint to all devices which match the selector. This has the same effect as if the taint was specified directly in the ResourceSlice by the DRA driver.

kinds.name: ResourceClaim
kinds.description:
ResourceClaim describes a request for access to resources in the cluster, for use by workloads. For example, if a workload needs an accelerator device with specific properties, this is how that request is expressed. The status stanza tracks whether this claim has been satisfied and what specific resources have been allocated.

This is an alpha type and requires enabling the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate.

kinds.name: ResourceClaimTemplate
kinds.description:
ResourceClaimTemplate is used to produce ResourceClaim objects.

kinds.description: PodGroup represents a runtime instance of pods grouped together. PodGroups are created by workload controllers (Job, LWS, JobSet, etc...) from Workload.podGroupTemplates. PodGroup API enablement is toggled by the GenericWorkload feature gate.

kinds.description: Workload allows for expressing scheduling constraints that should be used when managing the lifecycle of workloads from the scheduling perspective, including scheduling, preemption, eviction and other phases. Workload API enablement is toggled by the GenericWorkload feature gate.

kinds.name: PriorityClass
kinds.description: PriorityClass defines mapping from a priority class name to the priority integer value. The value can be any valid integer.

kinds.name: VolumeAttributesClass
kinds.description: VolumeAttributesClass represents a specification of mutable volume attributes defined by the CSI driver. The class can be specified during dynamic provisioning of PersistentVolumeClaims, and changed in the PersistentVolumeClaim spec after provisioning.

kinds.name: CSIDriver

CSIDriver objects are non-namespaced.

kinds.name: StorageClass
kinds.description:
StorageClass describes the parameters for a class of storage for which PersistentVolumes can be dynamically provisioned.

StorageClasses are non-namespaced; the name of the storage class according to etcd is in ObjectMeta.Name.

kinds.name: VolumeAttachment
kinds.description:
VolumeAttachment captures the intent to attach or detach the specified volume to/from the specified node.

VolumeAttachment objects are non-namespaced.
